stimulus.text:
| Group | Response to the Declaration |
| African Americans | Its natural-rights language seemed to challenge slavery. Jefferson's first draft blamed slavery on Britain, but Congress removed that passage. Some enslaved people fled to the British; some in the North won freedom by serving in the militia or the Continental Army. |
| Native Americans | Most supported the British, fearing the land hunger of the new nation. |
| Women | Revolutionary ideals inspired the idea of republican motherhood: women would educate their sons to be citizens of the republic, so mothers themselves needed education. |

books.section: B. Common Sense, the Declaration of Independence, and Republican Self-Government

options.text: The right of women to vote in the new republic's elections
options.misconception: Women did not gain the vote in the new republic. Republican motherhood was about education, not suffrage.

options.text: The duty of mothers to keep their sons out of the Continental Army entirely
options.misconception: The idea pointed the other way — mothers were to raise sons as citizens of the republic, not shield them from it.

options.text: That mothers should be educated to raise sons as citizens of the republic
The law requiring every mother to send her sons to a public school
options.misconception: Background: no law required mothers to send sons to public school — republican motherhood was an ideal, not a statute.

rationales.C: Mothers would educate their sons to be citizens, so mothers themselves needed education — that is republican motherhood. The duty to teach made the mother's own learning a public need.
rationales.A: The vote did not follow. Republican motherhood gave women an educational role, not the franchise.
rationales.B: Shielding sons from the army is the opposite of the idea. Mothers were to raise citizens for the republic.
rationales.D: No such law existed. Republican motherhood was a cultural ideal about women's education, not a statute.
rationales.general:
1. Read the table's row. Revolutionary ideals inspired the idea of republican motherhood.
2. Follow the chain. Sons must become citizens, mothers must teach them, so mothers must be educated.
3. Name the idea. A mother's education became a public duty, because her sons' citizenship depended on it.
Remember: an ideal that gives someone a new duty usually gives them a new reason to learn — here, mothers learned so sons could be citizens.
